'''''Anthurium andraeanum''''', also known as '''Édouard François André's Tailflower''', is a [[flowering plant]] species in the family [[Araceae]] that is native to [[Colombia]] and [[Ecuador]].<ref name=uiasidofuasodifoasdh>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=10633 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref> It is a winner of the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/1349/i-Anthurium-andraeanum-i/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder – ''Anthurium andraeanum'' | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | accessdate=12 January 2018}}</ref>

==Names==
[[Common name]]s for plants in the genus ''[[Anthurium]]'' include '''flamingo flower''', '''tailflower''', '''painter's palette''', '''oilcloth flower''', and '''laceleaf'''.<ref name=nc>[http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/poison/Anthusp.htm ''Anthurium'' spp.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131003023439/http://www.ces.ncsu.edu/depts/hort/consumer/poison/Anthusp.htm |date=2013-10-03 }} Poisonous Plants of North Carolina. North Carolina State University.</ref><ref>[https://www.itis.gov/servlet/SingleRpt/SingleRpt?search_topic=TSN&search_value=42558 ''Anthurium''.] ITIS.</ref><ref name="Govaerts, R. 2002"/><ref>Nadruz Coelho, M.A., Waechter, J.L. & Mayo, S.J. (2009). Revisão taxonômica das espécies de Anthurium (Araceae) seção Urospadix subseção Flavescentiviridia. Rodriguésia; Revista do Instituto de Biologia Vegetal, Jardim Botânico e Estaçao Biologica do Itatiaya 60: 799–864.</ref> Its name comes from the Greek words ''anthos'', meaning flower, and ''oura'', meaning a tail, referring to the spadix.<ref name=greeknaming>[http://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=b575"Anthurium Andraeanum." Missouri Botanical Garden]</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Anthurium andraeanum (5) 1200.jpg|thumb|left|Spathe closeup]]
It is a [[monocotyledonous]] [[perennial]], preferring warm, shady and humid climates, such as tropical rainforests.  Its most characteristic feature as an [[ornamental plant|ornamental]] is its brightly colored [[spathe]] leaf, and the protruding [[inflorescence]] called the [[spadix (botany)|spadix]].<ref name=details>Collette VE, Jameson PE, Schwinn KE, Umaharan P, Davies KM (2004) Temporal and spatial expression of flavonoid biosynthetic genes in flowers of Anthurium andraeanum. Physiol Plant 122:297–304. doi:10.1111/j.1399-3054.2004.00402.x</ref>

It is a short erected plant with whole, [[cardioid]] or heart-shaped leaves, generally reflexed, [[Cordate (leaf shape)|cordate]] base, apex acuminate or cuspid, which are borne by a cylindrical [[Petiole (botany)|petiole]] 30–40 cm long.

The spathe is cartilage-waxy, brightly coloured (red, pink) and 8–15 cm long, excluding the [[inflorescence]] (the [[Spadix (botany)|spadix]]), which is 7–9 cm long, similar to a candle-holder, white or yellow in colour, is erected, and bears many small [[hermaphroditic]] flowers. These include a [[perianth]] with four segments and [[stamens]] with a compressed mesh. Flowering extends throughout the year.<ref name="Govaerts, R. 2002">Govaerts, R. & Frodin, D.G. (2002). World Checklist and Bibliography of Araceae (and Acoraceae): 1–560. The Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew.</ref>

The fruit is a fleshy [[berry]].<ref>Linden ex André, Ill. Hort. 24: 43 (1877).</ref>

==Distribution==
Native to Ecuador and southwestern Colombia, it is also naturalised in other parts of the world. It is found in the [[Caribbean]] and [[Réunion]]. It is grown as an [[ornamental plant]] in the form of many hybrids or horticultural varieties. It is commonly used to make [[Flower bouquet|bouquet]]s.

==Toxicity==
The whole plant is [[toxic]]. It contains [[saponin]]s and crystals of [[calcium oxalate]], in fine needles, able to penetrate the [[mucous membrane]]s and provokes painful irritations. It is toxic to all mammals: a mouth-worn fragment can cause severe irritation of the mouth and throat. Contact with a human causes [[erythema]], [[blister]]s, and if ingested, [[salivation]], difficulty in swallowing and vomiting.<ref>Jacques Fournet, Flora illustrated the flowering of Guadeloupe and Martinique, Gondwana editions, CIRAD2002 Volume 1 ({{ISBN|2-87614-489-1}}); Volume 2 ({{ISBN|2-87614-492-1}})</ref>
